scope: Native TCP SACK permission admission. Synthetic file-only inline DAQ verdicts and byte-preservation checks; no live interface, installation or deployment.
changes: SID 9201018 and ax_tcp_sack_state require the peer admitted SACK-Permitted SYN offer, both observed handshake directions, ACK without SYN, and an established native TCP flow before admitting SACK.

Bounded state is owned by each native TCP flow; original wire-context pending offers commit only after admission. Rejected grant/revocation attempts do not change permission, and reset/reused or independent connections start without permission.

Completed fragment flows lack the pinned engine final-verdict event. A later context-cleanup backstop admits the offer only on the flowless PASS/REPLACE-equivalent path, excluding trust, drop, hold, retry, injection and aborted cleanup.

Admitted conflicting retransmissions can narrow permission but cannot restore it. This is explicit strict local ambiguity policy, not an assertion that RFC 2018 prohibits every changed retransmission.

baseline.scope: Synthetic inline file replay only. SID 9202999 is a fixture-only drop of valid handshake offers; it is not part of the deployed ruleset.

replay.scope: Synthetic inline file replay only. SID 9202999 is a fixture-only drop of valid handshake offers; it is not part of the deployed ruleset.

sanitized_replay.scope: Synthetic inline file replay only. SID 9202999 is a fixture-only drop of valid handshake offers; it is not part of the deployed ruleset.

initial_guard_findings.cause: Completed fragment flows were removed before the flow-gated FINALIZE_PACKET callback, so admitted fragmented offers were not committed.
initial_guard_findings.repair: The final plugin adds the release-pinned packet-context cleanup backstop. All 344 original input conversations and their admission expectations are unchanged.

nd_validation_test: 206 assertions and 100000 deterministic randomized cases passed
ip_validation_test: 535904 IP framing assertions and 100000 deterministic randomized cases passed
ip4_options_test: 1177304 assertions and 100000 deterministic randomized cases passed
ip6_options_test: 2168 IPv6 option assertions and 100000 randomized cases passed
esp_validation_test: 6920 ESP framing assertions and 100000 deterministic randomized cases passed
routing_validation_test: 3253 Routing Type 2 assertions and 100000 randomized cases passed
home_address_test: 306943 Home Address assertions, 100000 semantic cases and 100000 arbitrary spans passed
tcp_options_test: 1499749 assertions and 100000 deterministic randomized cases passed
tcp_sack_state_test: 100000 deterministic randomized connection histories passed
parser_build.scope: Build and pure-parser checks only. Load and PCAP replay must be validated separately.

instrumented_plugin_build.scope: Address/undefined-instrumented protocol plugin; unchanged instrumented perimeter library; separately built AddressSanitizer engine.

profiles.scope: Native configuration loading and effective rule states only; no traffic or live inline enforcement.

dns_profiles.scope: Configuration and effective rule states only; not packet forwarding or deployment.

notes: Analyzer performs Active::execute and distill_verdict before the final event. Completed fragment flows are released before the event gate; pkth is cleared before DAQ finalization, followed by ContextSwitcher::stop and context-data cleanup while Active remains available.

Active::session_was_allowed includes trust, so the backstop explicitly rejects session_was_trusted in addition to packet/decode trust, resized packet injection, pending conflict, wrong packet number or a remaining flow.
Named FlowData pins the plugin. Shared ownership keeps bounded pending state alive if native flow cleanup occurs during processing. Native reset cleanup releases connection state.

Global final-event registration and the flowless cleanup backstop depend on this pinned lifecycle and existing subscribers. Additional verdict-changing plugins or another engine release require re-audit. Live plugin replacement is not declared supported.

limitations: This change enforces observed SACK permission; it does not authenticate peers, validate SACK block sequence truth or implement every TCP extension negotiation.

344 selected native conversations and 100000 randomized connection histories are counted once. Probe/baseline/prototype runs, 344 instrumented repetitions, 3540 existing regression cases, fixed assertions and repeated parser builds are excluded from the combined increment.
The full engine is AddressSanitizer-instrumented; the protocol plugin and pure parser/state tests additionally use UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer. Whole-engine UBSan coverage is not asserted.
SID 9202999 is a fixture-only rejection rule used to exercise rejected handshake offers. It is excluded from production rule totals.

Current rules require the rebuilt plugin alongside the previously repaired, pinned Snort 3.12.2.0 engine. Live plugin replacement is unsupported; restart the configured engine when replacing the plugin.
Evidence is local macOS arm64 and file-only inline DAQ replay. Linux runtime behavior, deployed sandbox routing, universal RFC/W3C compliance and prevention of all unknown attacks remain unproved.
